extractions.description: Introduces and evaluates GRIT, a graph Transformer with learned relative random-walk positional encodings, pair-aware attention, and degree scaling, on graph-learning benchmarks and synthetic attention experiments.

type.quote: Along with theoretical justification, we provide ample empirical evidence to demonstrate the effectiveness of our design choices.
type.justification: The paper includes proofs, but its principal claims are tested through benchmark, ablation, sensitivity, runtime, and synthetic experiments.

name.justification: The paper proposes an advance specifically for this research area.
